title: Draw a map of your app's parts with your coding agent
summary: A solo builder ran the Archify add-on in Claude Code on their app; it drew the system, growing from 15 parts and 14 links to 17 and 19.
agent_role: The agent read the code and drew a diagram of the whole system, with each box linked to its source lines. The human uses the diagram to vet new features.
outcome: Author reports the map grew from 15 parts and 14 links on Oct 9 to 17 parts and 19 links on Oct 21. They now check what a new feature touches before adding it.
what_they_did: The poster had spent 12 days building their app, Airsc, one prompt at a time. By then it had payments, a daily quota, an X bot and admin pages. They ran Archify, an add-on for Claude Code, on the code to draw the whole system.
how_it_went: They say the diagram linked each box to its source lines. It went from 15 parts and 14 links on Oct 9 to 17 parts and 19 links on Oct 21.
worth_knowing: They now check what each new feature touches before letting it into the app. The add-on was built by another person, @t20000622yy.
prompt: Read the code in [project folder] and draw a diagram of the whole system. Show its main parts, how they connect, and the files and lines behind each part. Save it as [diagram file]. Then, for the feature I'm planning, [feature description], list which parts and connections it would touch. Flag any new connections it would add.

curation.rationale: A real use of a Claude Code add-on to map a fast-growing app, with simple before/after numbers. It is brief and partly promotes the tool's maker.
